why: Two levels of the same idea: binary search the speed k, and inside, a greedy feasibility check that packs consecutive orders into each rider's hour budget and counts riders. Faster speeds never need more riders, so the search is valid.
hints: At a fixed speed k every order becomes a whole number of hours. What is left is a packing question.

Greedy: give the current rider orders in sequence while their hours fit in hoursPerRider, then start a new rider. If some single order needs more than hoursPerRider hours, k fails outright. Riders needed is non-increasing in k.
Binary search the smallest k in [1, max(workloads)] with ridersNeeded(k) <= riders. O(n log max).
pitfalls: An order that alone exceeds hoursPerRider makes k infeasible no matter how riders are used.
This is the capacity-to-ship check with ceil(w / k) as the weights; reuse that structure.
